kinds.d: Copper silicate hydroxide specimen: intense emerald-green to teal rhombohedral crystals, from Tsumeb, Congo and Kazakhstan.

x.d: Finest dioptase specimens, from Tsumeb, Namibia, the most famous and expensive locality.
x.dt: green crystals on matrix · miniature to cabinet

x.d: Classic dioptase from Renéville, Republic of the Congo.
Original discovery site in Karagandy, Kazakhstan; named dioptase by Haüy in 1797.
Dioptase from the Mammoth-Saint Anthony mine near Mammoth and the Christmas mine near Hayden.
Dioptase from Tantara and the Mashamba West mine, Kolwezi.

kinds.d: Hydrated copper silicate specimen: blue-green botryoidal masses and crusts; hard silica-rich types are cut as gems.

x.d: Vivid blue and blue-green chrysocolla, used in place of turquoise in silver and gold work.
Heavily silicified chrysocolla reaching hardness about 7.
Chrysocolla from the Ray mine, Pinal County, Arizona.
Chrysocolla from Bisbee, Arizona.
Chrysocolla from the Timna (King Solomon's) mine, Israel.
Chrysocolla from the Star of the Congo mine, Lubumbashi, and Likasi.

kinds.d: Potassium calcium silicate specimen: swirling lilac to violet fibrous rock found only in the Murun massif, Sakha, Siberia.

x.d: Charoite from the Murun Massif, Aldan Shield, Sakha, the only reported locality; known from the 1940s and described in 1978.
Named after the Chara River, about 70 km from the discovery site.

kinds.d: Potassium sodium lithium iron manganese silicate specimen: purple massive stone from the Wessels mine, South Africa; type locality Iwagi, Japan.

x.d: Gem sugilite from the Wessels Mine, Northern Cape, South Africa, in a strata-bound manganese deposit.
Type-locality sugilite from Iwagi Islet, Japan, described in 1944 by Ken-ichi Sugi; not good for jewellery.
Alternative name for sugilite among collectors, also lavulite or royal azel.

kinds.d: Zinc silicate specimen: fluorescent green under shortwave UV; the Franklin, New Jersey specimens are classic.

x.d: Willemite from Franklin and Sterling Hill, New Jersey, strongly green-fluorescent, often with calcite.
Manganese-bearing brown willemite.
Willemite from the Mammoth-St. Anthony and Red Cloud mines.
Type-locality willemite from the Vieille-Montagne mine, Belgium, found in 1829 and named for William I of the Netherlands.
Willemite from Tsumeb and Guchab, Namibia.

kinds.d: Sodium calcium iron zirconium silicate specimen: red to magenta masses and crystals from nepheline syenites.

x.d: Red eudialyte from the Khibiny and Lovozero massifs, Kola Peninsula.
Eudialyte from the Ilimaussaq complex, Greenland.
Eudialyte from Mont Saint-Hilaire, Quebec.
Eudialyte from Poços de Caldas, Brazil.
Eudialyte from Magnet Cove, Arkansas, and Pajarito Mountain, New Mexico.

kinds.d: Calcium titanium silicate specimen: wedge-shaped brown, yellow and green crystals, also called sphene; fiery gem.

x.d: Informal name for gem titanite, prized for dispersion exceeding diamond's; IMA discredited sphene in 1982.
Titanite crystals from Tavetsch, St Gotthard, Zermatt and the Zillertal.
Gem titanite from Pakistan and Madagascar.
Large titanite crystals from the Dodo mine, Subpolar Urals.

kinds.d: Calcium manganese silicate hydrate specimen: rose-red to orange fibrous sprays, notably from the Kalahari manganese field.

x.d: Inesite from the N'Chwaning and Wessels mines, Kalahari Manganese Field.
Inesite from Långban, Värmland, Sweden.
Inesite from Quinault and the Crescent mine, Olympic Peninsula.
Inesite from the Equity mine, near Creede, Colorado.

kinds.d: Hydrated calcium silicate specimen: colourless to white prismatic crystals, first found in 1925 at Dutoitspan, Kimberley.

x.d: Type-locality afwillite from the Dutoitspan mine, Kimberley, South Africa, discovered in 1925.
Afwillite from Crestmore quarry, Riverside County, California.
Afwillite from Scawt Hill, Co. Antrim.
Afwillite from the Wessels mine, Kuruman.

notes: All 9 planned kinds kept. HOM has no charoite file (404); Wikipedia used. Sources: Wikipedia plus HOM for the others. Eilat stone, gem silica and Hotazel/Royal Purple sugilite are not on fetched pages so omitted. No brands or traditions.
